svg.text: Revision 2.0 · 2026-08-27 · authoritative netlist = HARDWARE.md §6 · BLE frame layout = lib/core/services/ble_protocol.dart
micro-USB 5 V in · Rprog 1.2 k = 1 A charge
3.3 V / 2 A · flat rail from 4.2 V down to 2.5 V
NEVER an LDO from a bare cell — see errata E1
GND RAIL ← star point at U9 GND
4.2 V → 2.10 V · 3.0 V → 1.50 V · 21 µA drain · avg 64 samples
NEVER take an ECG while USB charger is connected.
A charger ties the patient's electrodes to mains earth
through this unisolated board. Firmware enforces it:
dual core 240 MHz · BLE 4.2 · 4 MB flash
core 0: 250 Hz ECG ISR + DSP | core 1: BLE notify
→ every analog input is on ADC1: GPIO32–39
U2 AD8232 single-lead ECG front end
0.5 Hz 2-pole HP · 40 Hz LP · gain ≈ 100 · RLD feedback
LO+ → GPIO39 push-pull, HIGH = lead off
GND: own wire to U9 star point — do NOT daisy-chain
RA / LA / RL → 3.5 mm TRS → 3-lead snap cable
sampled 250 Hz by hardware timer ISR · 50 Hz notch (India)
red+IR reflectance · 100 Hz · 411 µs pulse · FIFO int
SEPARATE BUS — breakout pull-ups reference 1.8 V (E5)
add NO external pull-ups here · perfusion index < 0.2 → SpO₂ = 0
fingertip clip, opaque shroud, 40 cm tether
100 kHz is set by the MLX90614's SMBus timing, not the fastest device
pull-ups: 4.7 kΩ to 3V3 — ONE pair only
desolder the onboard pull-ups from 3 of the 4 breakouts
4 × 4.7 k in parallel = 1.18 kΩ → bus works only sometimes (§7.2)
IR skin temp · BAA ±0.5 °C/90° FOV · DCI ±0.2 °C/5° FOV (E2)
±8 g · INT → GPIO33, active HIGH push-pull, RTC wake (E3)
T / RH / P — verify chip ID 0xD0 == 0x60, not 0x58 (BMP280)
SW1 polarity is INVERTED on purpose (§6.7)
pressed = HIGH. ext1 with two sources supports only
ANY_HIGH, so IMU_INT and BTN_MAIN must both be active-high.
SW2 → GPIO13, switch to GND, INPUT_PULLUP
BZ1 → GPIO25 via 1 kΩ + BC547, LEDC 2 kHz
PMS5003 PM2.5 → UART2 GPIO16 RX / GPIO17 TX, 9600 8N1
needs 5 V @ ~100 mA — tap BEFORE the 3.3 V regulator, never 3V3
duty-cycle via SET pin: fan needs 30 s to stabilise
DS3231 RTC @ 0x68→0x57 conflict: use 0x68 bus slot carefully
ATT MTU stays at the 23-byte default →
20 B payload − 4 B hdr = 16 B = 8 × int16
9 samples → every ECG frame silently dropped
9 u8 flags b0 Rpeak b1 fall
on 'EXPERIMENTAL', so the cuffless BP estimate adds
ZERO to the risk score. Ship it that way (§15).
PTT is a real measurement worth transmitting.
SBP/DBP without per-subject cuff calibration is not.
The board never computes a risk band. Ever.
Fall detection — match the app exactly (§17.2)
porting its constants means those tests document the firmware too.
idle → freeFall → awaitingImpact → FALL. A bare impact spike
with no preceding free fall is NOT a fall — that gate is what stops
"phone set down hard" firing an SOS several times an hour.
Deep sleep — the claim a phone cannot make (§5.2, §17.3)
MPU6050 motion int in cycle mode ≈ 10 µA · AD8232 SDN low · MAX30102 shutdown · OLED off
Total ≈ 25 µA → ≈ 11 months of fall-watch standby on one 3000 mAh cell.
Streaming 130 mA ≈ 19.8 h · monitoring 63 mA ≈ 40 h · idle 26 mA ≈ 99 h
Use the MPU6050's MOTION interrupt as a wake trigger only — its built-in free-fall bit is unreliable. Classify on the ESP32.
Bring-up order (§16) — each step must pass before soldering the next:
1 power stage alone (verify 3.30 V at a 3.4 V cell) → 2 bulk caps → 3 ESP32 blink → 4 OLED → 5 MLX → 6 MPU → 7 BME
8 re-measure bus pull-up → 9 I²C1 + MAX30102 → 10-11 AD8232 → 12 I/O → 13 BLE → 14 ECG stream → 15 deep sleep < 100 µA
